summary: DiskWhy phase J: backend (fast/honest/stoppable cleanup) in parallel with layout & clarity frontend

result.rMain:
Lane R is finished: the backend compiles, and `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` passes (107 passed, 0 failed). `cargo build --release -p diskwhy` builds cleanly.

Two things are compiled but were not tested end to end. `elevate_quarantine` needs a real UAC click, though the elevated helper's early exit was run (codes below). The close guard needs real mouse input.

## Files changed (my lane only)
- `crates/diskwhy-core/Cargo.toml`: adds the windows-sys feature `Win32_Security_Authorization`.
- `crates/diskwhy-core/src/action/`:
  - `mod.rs`: Strategy::Permanent, Dest, CountBytes, ByDest, SkipReason::Hardlink, Plan.safe_direct.
  - `execute.rs`: rewritten.
  - `perf.rs`: new, the time-estimate model.
  - `runstate.rs`: new, `last-run.json`.
  - `winops.rs`, `quarantine.rs`, `preflight.rs`, `log.rs`, `plan.rs`.
- Tests: `tests/action_tests.rs` (7 new tests; existing quarantine/recycle tests now set `plan.safe_direct = false`; the log line count gains the `start` record). New `tests/bench_tests.rs` (`#[ignore]`, run by hand).
- `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`.

No files outside my lane need changing.

## What the backend now does
- **Deletion method:** "可放心清理" (safe) items with `safe_direct` are deleted directly. The file is opened with DELETE access without following links, its fingerprint is re-checked on that same handle, then it is marked for deletion. Read-only files are deleted too. Everything else follows the chosen strategy. All 9 guardrails run before any method. Execution also re-checks for files that became cloud files after the preflight.
- **Work queue:** all items are cut into 256-entry chunks in one interleaved queue, using `clamp(CPUs, 4, 16)` threads with 8 MB stacks. The thread that finishes an item's last chunk removes its empty folders and saves the manifest. Manifests are also saved every 10 s.
- **Whole-folder recycle:** on by default (`DIR_RECYCLE`), only in recycle-bin mode, only through the strict gate; otherwise it falls back to per-file. The log still has one record per file plus one `recycle_dir` record per folder. Tests cover both the whole-folder path and the fallback when a file appears after the preflight.
- **Cross-drive quarantine:** copies with `CopyFileExW` and can be interrupted; the half-copied file is removed. Hard-linked files are skipped with 「硬链接，删了不腾空间」.
- **Stop:** remaining files are left untouched and counted in `not_processed`. Only folders that are truly empty are removed. Tested: 376 done, 2,624 untouched, and exactly 2,624 files still on disk.
- **Interrupted runs:** `actions.log` gets a `start` record and a `heartbeat` every 30 s. `last-run.json` tracks the run. The log is rotated above 50 MB.
- **Recycle-bin usage:** read by listing the current user's `$Recycle.Bin\<SID>` folder. `SHQueryRecycleBinW` took 23 s on your 260k-item bin; the listing takes 0.45 s and gives the identical byte count. The capacity check runs only for the full preflight, not the quick estimate.
- **Quarantine folder:** new batches go to `DiskWhy暂存区`. `list_batches` and `purge` still find old `DiskWhy-Quarantine` batches. Manifests are now written compact.

## Contract for the frontend (names as serialized)

**Changed command:**
- `preview_plan(items, strategy, safeDirect?: boolean, onEvent)`.
- `safeDirect` defaults to true; pass false when the user explicitly picks 回收站.
- `strategy` can now also be `{kind:"permanent"}`.

**New commands:**
- `cancel_execute() -> boolean`: true if an execution was running.
- `action_status() -> boolean`: whether an execute/restore/purge is running (for after a page reload).
- `last_interrupted() -> null | {batch: string, started: number, processed: number, processed_bytes: number, total: number}`.
- `dismiss_interrupted() -> null`.
- `prepare_quarantine(driveRoot: "D:\\") -> {status:"ok", dest_root: string} | {status:"needs_elevation"} | {status:"failed", message: string}`.
  - The `dest_root` goes straight into `{kind:"quarantine", dest_root}`.
  - It may be a previously used folder rather than the drive root.
- `elevate_quarantine(driveRoot)`: same return shape. "你取消了授权" comes back as `failed`.

**New event:** `close-blocked`, payload `null`. It fires when the window close is blocked because an execution is running.

**ExecProgress** (`execute_plan` onProgress, about every 200 ms plus a final event):
```
{done, total, bytes_done, total_bytes, cost_done: f64, cost_total: f64, elapsed_ms, current: string, cancelling: bool}
```
The bar is `cost_done / cost_total`, which only goes up.

**ExecReport** (`ExecOutcome.report`), new fields:
- `freed_bytes`: measured from free space on each source drive before and after.
- `by_dest: {permanent:{count,bytes}, recycle:{count,bytes}, quarantine:{count,bytes}}`.
- `skipped_bytes`.
- `skipped_by_reason: {code: {count, bytes}}`. Codes: hot, cloud, locked, no_permission, protected, changed, missing, unreadable, hardlink.
- `failed_bytes`, `not_processed: {count, bytes}`, `duration_ms`, `safe_direct`, `workers`, `measured` (internal timing, ignore).
- `cancelled` is now really set when stopped.

Each item in `items[]` also gains `skipped_bytes`, `failed_bytes`, `by_dest`, `not_processed`, `not_processed_bytes`. Each entry in `details[]` gains `dest_kind: "permanent"|"recycle"|"quarantine"|null`.

**PreflightReport**, new fields:
- `safe_direct`.
- `est_secs: f64`. It is 0 while `pending` is true; show it only after the full check.
- `by_dest` as above. While `pending`, counts are 0 and bytes come from scan-time sizes.
- `skipped_bytes`, `skipped_by_reason: {code: {count, bytes}}`.
- `scan_total_bytes`: equals the quick estimate's `total_bytes`, so the UI can explain e.g. 30.1 → 29.3 GB.
- `quarantine_choices[]` gains `dest_root: string | null` (null means call `prepare_quarantine`).

**New warning code:** `recycle_over_capacity` (does not block). `recycle_low_space` now appears only when something actually goes to the recycle bin.

## Test results
```
diskwhy-core unit 18 passed | action_tests 36 passed | dedup 5 passed (1 ignored, pre-existing)
explain 34 | mock 8 | real_fs 6 | bench_tests 0 passed, 1 ignored
```
The new tests cover:
- Permanent delete honours protected paths (checked at execution time), hot files, files locked at preflight and at execution, changed fingerprints, cloud files at preflight and at execution, and links (link removed, target hash unchanged).
- Safe items go direct while review items go to quarantine.
- Stop, folder recycle with fallback, cross-drive hardlink skip and copy cancel.
- The quarantine fallback chain and old-name batches.
- Log rotation and recycle-bin capacity reading.

The cross-drive tests used `DISKWHY_TEST_XVOL_DIR=D:\desk\claudex\13\dw-test-xvol`.

## Benchmark (release build, data on D:, `bench_tests.rs`)

| Method | Files | Threads | Time | Files/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent delete | 200,070 | 16 | 11.96 s | 16,724 |
| Permanent delete | 20,000 | 1 | 4.08 s | 4,901 |
| Same-drive quarantine | 200,070 | 16 | 38.15 s | 5,244 |
| Recycle, whole folder | 800 | 2 | 0.30 s | 2,624 |
| Recycle, per file | 600 | 3 | 1.81 s | 332 |
| Recycle, per file | 600 | 1 | 2.70 s | 222 |
| Cross-drive C:→D: (small files) | 2,000 | 8 | 2.18 s | 916 |

- Purging the 200k quarantine batch took 29 s.
- Compared with the old engine on your machine (about 85 files/s on a single item, 185 overall), permanent delete is roughly 90× faster than the old overall rate. Whole-folder recycle is about 14× and same-drive quarantine about 28×.
- I ran recycle mode on only 2,000 files. Everything was moved back out of the D: bin, and a final scan found none of the test's items left in either the C: or D: bin.
- All test folders I created were removed. `D:\desk\claudex\13\dw-wmi` is not mine and was left alone.

**Estimate defaults** (`perf.rs`, single-thread cost per file, calibrated from the runs above; they differ from the plan's starting values):

| Method | Plan said | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Permanent delete | 0.1 ms | 0.20 ms |
| Same-drive rename | 0.2 ms | 0.65 ms |
| Recycle bin | 2 ms | 4.0 ms |
| Cross-drive | 1 ms | 3.0 ms (150 MB/s throughput kept) |
| Empty-folder removal | — | 0.1 ms |

- Parallel speedup follows Amdahl's law with a serial fraction of 0.25, measured from 16 threads being only 3.4× faster.
- With these values the estimates match the measured runs within about 5% for permanent delete, quarantine and cross-drive.
- After each real run the model rescales the operations it actually did toward the measured time and saves to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DiskWhy\perf.json`.

## Not done or uncertain
- **`elevate_quarantine` end to end:** not run, because it needs someone to click the UAC prompt. The helper's arguments were checked on the real exe before any window opens: bad arguments exit with 2, and non-elevated with your real SID exits with 3 (no folder created). Your account is an admin with a limited token, so it gets `needs_elevation`. The test also confirms D:\ root is not writable, so the chain falls back to a previously used folder.
- **Close guard:** compiled only, not exercised. JS `close()` does fire `CloseRequested` according to the Tauri source.
- **Recycle hang risk:** an oversize file going to the recycle bin can still raise an invisible confirmation box that hangs a worker. This is the crash doc's item 2, and I left that flag unchanged. Safe items no longer go to the bin and whole-folder recycle is capped at 1 GB, which shrinks but does not remove the risk.
- **Not done in this lane:** the panic hook, minidump and WebView2 process-failure handling from the crash doc.
- **Per-file safety check:** the protected-path check during execution still resolves each file's parent folder without a cache, deliberately for safety. It is part of the 0.2 ms per file.
result.rHarden:
I've finished the R-lane hardening pass. `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` passes (119 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, both expected) and `cargo build --release -p diskwhy` builds. I also checked the main fixes on the real exe, not just in tests.

**What I checked on the real exe**
- **Close guard:** I used the debug build with a debug-only hook that keeps it in the "executing" state. A plain window-close message and the Alt+F4 / taskbar close message were both blocked, the process stayed alive, and each was logged in crash.log. The ✕ button calls `close()` from JS; per the Tauri source that goes through the same close-request path, but I couldn't click it myself.
- **WebView2 crash:** killing the window's WebView2 browser process now leaves DiskWhy running. It logs the failure, rebuilds the window, starts a new browser and renderer, and the rebuilt window is still close-guarded. When not executing, a normal close still exits with code 0.
- **Comparison with the old build:** killing the browser of the old `DiskWhy-app\DiskWhy.exe` does not make it exit (still alive after 15 s, presumably a blank window). So a WebView2 crash alone doesn't explain your mid-cleanup exit. It's consistent with an outside kill, or with you closing a blank window via the taskbar or Alt+F4, which the old build didn't block.

**One thing found along the way:** your real DiskWhy (pid 84436) is running and shares its WebView2 browser process with any new instance. My tests used a separate WebView2 data folder (`WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER`) and never touched your instance.

**Files outside crates/ and src-tauri/src I edited, please confirm:**
- Root `Cargo.toml`: release profile now keeps line-number debug info, no stripping, separate `.pdb`. This is what makes crash backtraces readable.
  - Size: the exe is 12.6 MB, plus a 31.9 MB `diskwhy.pdb` next to it.
  - It's worth copying the `.pdb` with the exe.
  - The release build took 4 min 39 s.
- `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`: adds `webview2-com` and `windows-core` (same versions Tauri already uses).
- `Cargo.lock`: dependency lists only, no new packages.

**Changes, by item in the crash doc and your list**
- **Crash logging (new `crates/diskwhy-core/src/crash.rs`):**
  - Panics are written to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DiskWhy\crash.log` with message, location, thread name and backtrace, then the default behaviour runs.
  - Unhandled native exceptions write a minidump to `crash\diskwhy-<UTC time>-<pid>.dmp` plus one log line. Per Microsoft's docs, the dump is written by a dedicated pre-started thread, with no allocation in the handler, then handed back to the default handler.
  - The log rotates above 2 MB; the 5 newest dumps are kept.
  - Execution worker threads are now named `exec-N`.
- **Close guard:**
  - `acting` is now reset automatically on any exit path, including a panic, so it can't stay stuck on.
  - Safety valve: if Stop was pressed and work still hasn't ended after 20 s, the close is allowed so the window can never become unclosable.
  - Blocked closes and exit requests during execution are logged.
- **WebView2 recovery:**
  - Browser process died: rebuild the window.
  - Page renderer died: reload.
  - Renderer unresponsive about 1 minute: reload.
  - Anything else: log only.
- **Recycle bin hang:**
  - Removed `FOF_WANTNUKEWARNING`, the invisible-dialog risk.
  - Files bigger than that drive's recycle bin limit, or on a drive where "delete directly" is set, are skipped before sending, as new skip code `recycle_unavailable`, and left untouched.
  - Per-file results now come from the shell's progress callback. A file locked after the pre-check is reported as "skipped · in use" instead of "you clicked No". If Windows still deletes something outright, it's reported honestly as a direct delete with a note.
  - `SetOwnerWindow` and message pumping aren't needed now, because no dialog can appear.
- **Running Chromium/Electron caches:** a cache folder that a running program has open is skipped as "in use". This is detected via Restart Manager even when the program allows deletion. Normally this is one query; a test with one open cache took 0.29 s.
- **DiskWhy's own data protected:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DiskWhy` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.diskwhy.desktop` (its WebView2 data) can no longer be deleted.
- **Evidence for interrupted runs:**
  - The log `start` record now has the parent process and exe path.
  - A `batch_begin` line is written before each 256-file block.
  - `last-run.json` records the exe.
  - On the next launch, the interrupted-run notice includes the Windows exit code. It's read from the Program Compatibility Assistant log, and the parser was tested on your machine's real `0x8f` line.
  - It also says whether a crash was logged.
- **Rejected:** running cleanup in a separate child process (item 4). It's a large architecture change, and the close guard plus WebView2 recovery cover what was observed.
- **Already done by the main implementer:** heartbeat, log rotation, 8 MB stacks, whole-folder recycle.

**Tests added (all passing)**
- `crash_tests` (4): panic hook output; access violation producing a valid minidump plus log line.
- 5 new in `action_tests`: per-file recycle results (locked file gave HRESULT 0x80270027), locked after pre-check counts as skipped, an oversized sparse file is refused and left in place, live cache skipped, own data protected.
- PCA log parsing; the close-guard and stuck-flag safety valve.
- One existing log test updated for the new `batch_begin` line.

**Not verified**
- Clicking ✕ itself, which needs real mouse input.
- Panic backtraces in the release build (tested in debug only).
- A minidump from inside the actual app (tested via a test process).
- `elevate_quarantine`, which needs a UAC click.

**Remaining risk**
- An app that starts between the pre-check and execution can still lose its "safe" cache files to direct deletion.
- If the rebuilt window never starts loading, exit stays blocked.

**Cleanup:** my test folders are deleted and none of my test items are left in the C: or D: recycle bins. Two `%TEMP%\diskwhy-act-*` folders from 14:29 and 14:40 are from the earlier implementer run, so I left them.

## Full contract for the frontend
Arguments are camelCase from JS.

**Commands**
- `preview_plan(items, strategy, safeDirect?: boolean, onEvent)` → PreflightReport.
  - `safeDirect` defaults to true; pass false when the user explicitly picks 回收站.
  - `strategy` is one of `{kind:"recycle_bin"}`, `{kind:"quarantine", dest_root}`, `{kind:"permanent"}`.
- `execute_plan(planId, skipLocked, onProgress)` → `{report: ExecReport, refresh, summary}`.
- `cancel_execute()` → boolean (true if an execution was running).
- `action_status()` → boolean (whether an execute / restore / purge is running).
- **New:** `exec_progress()` → `ExecProgress | null`. Latest progress while executing, for re-attaching after a reload or window rebuild.
- **New:** `last_exec_report()` → `ExecReport | null`. Most recent report in this run of the app.
- `last_interrupted()` → `null | {batch: string, started: number, processed: number, processed_bytes: number, total: number, exit_code: string | null, crash_logged: boolean}`.
  - `exit_code` and `crash_logged` are new.
  - It returns null while something is running.
- `dismiss_interrupted()` → null.
- **New:** `log_frontend_error(message: string, stack?: string, source?: string)` → null.
  - Hook it to window `error` and `unhandledrejection`.
  - Limited to 200 entries per run, 4000 characters each.
- `prepare_quarantine(driveRoot)` and `elevate_quarantine(driveRoot)` → `{status:"ok", dest_root: string} | {status:"needs_elevation"} | {status:"failed", message: string}`.
  - "你取消了授权" comes back as `failed`.

**Event:** `close-blocked`, payload null. Emitted when ✕, Alt+F4 or taskbar close is blocked during execution; not emitted once the 20 s safety valve allows the close.

**ExecProgress** (about every 200 ms, plus a final event):
- `{done, total, bytes_done, total_bytes, cost_done: f64, cost_total: f64, elapsed_ms, current: string, cancelling: bool}`
- The bar is `cost_done / cost_total`, which only goes up.

**ExecReport**
- Existing fields: `batch_id, strategy_label, started_at, finished_at, items[], ok, ok_bytes, skipped, failed, manifest_path, log_path, log_failures, cancelled, affected_dirs[], notes[]`.
- Added this phase:
  - `freed_bytes`: free space measured on each source drive before and after.
  - `by_dest: {permanent:{count,bytes}, recycle:{count,bytes}, quarantine:{count,bytes}}`
  - `skipped_bytes`, `skipped_by_reason: {code: {count, bytes}}`, `failed_bytes`
  - `not_processed: {count, bytes}`, `duration_ms`, `safe_direct`, `workers`
  - `measured`: internal timing, ignore.
- Each `items[]` entry adds: `skipped_bytes, failed_bytes, by_dest, not_processed, not_processed_bytes`.
- Each `details[]` entry adds: `dest_kind: "permanent" | "recycle" | "quarantine" | null`.
- If Windows deleted a recycle-bin file outright: that entry is `result:"ok"`, `dest_kind:"permanent"`, with a reason text, and `notes` gets a line saying so.

**Skip codes** (both reports): `hot, cloud, locked, no_permission, protected, changed, missing, unreadable, hardlink`, plus **new** `recycle_unavailable`.
- The serialized reason is `{kind:"recycle_unavailable", why}`.
- Suggested label: 回收站放不下.
- `locked` now also covers live Chromium/Electron caches, with process names.

**PreflightReport** new fields:
- `safe_direct`
- `est_secs: f64`: 0 while `pending` is true; show it only after the full check.
- `by_dest`: while `pending`, counts are 0 and bytes come from scan-time sizes.
- `skipped_bytes`, `skipped_by_reason: {code: {count, bytes}}`
- `scan_total_bytes`: equals the quick estimate's total, so the UI can explain e.g. 30.1 → 29.3 GB.
- `quarantine_choices[].dest_root: string | null`; null means call `prepare_quarantine`.
- Warning codes: `recycle_over_capacity` (does not block); `recycle_low_space` now appears only when something actually goes to the recycle bin.

**What the frontend lane needs to wire up**
- On load, call `action_status()`. If it's true, re-attach with `exec_progress()`; when it turns false, read the result with `last_exec_report()`.
- Register `log_frontend_error` for `error` and `unhandledrejection`.
- Add the `recycle_unavailable` label.
- Use `exit_code` and `crash_logged` in the interrupted-run notice if wanted.

F2 is finished: decisions 6–9, the 隔离区 → 暂存区 rename, the drive name taken from the scanned root, and the provider presets. `npm test` and `npm run build` both pass. A few things don't fully work yet: the Kimi preset will fail until the backend stops sending `temperature`, and some new heading characters in theme C fall back to a different font until the font subset is rebuilt. Both fixes are outside my lane and are listed below.

**Files changed (all inside my lane, plus two new files)**
- `src/store.ts`, navigation only:
  - `openDir(path, focusPath?)` auto-drills into the biggest folder only the first time (`listing === null`). After that, no `focusPath` means the right list shows the opened folder itself.
  - `setFocus(path)`: an empty path, or one equal to the opened folder (case and trailing `\` ignored), sets `focus = listing` and `focusKey = null`.
  - `enterBlock(p)` now calls `openDir(p, p)`.
  - New `switchDrive(root: string): Promise<void>`: if a scan is running it calls `doCancel()`, waits until `phase !== "scanning"`, clears the cancel error, then sets `scanRoot`, goes to the home page and calls `doScan()`.
  - Other store functions are untouched.
- `src/treemap.ts`: new `samePath(a, b): boolean` and `crumbTarget(bc, i): {open, focus} | null` (level 0 → the drive root for both; level i → open level i‑1, select level i).
